skill.name: commit-message-generator
skill.description: Drafts English Conventional Commit messages from Git status and diff output.
skill.summary: Turn Git diffs into focused Conventional Commit suggestions.
skill.author: Daisuke897

security_audit.summary: The four static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around Git commands. The skill uses fixed Git inspection commands to build commit suggestions and explicitly forbids running commit or push. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Run `git status` to check modified files
2. Retrieve diffs with `git diff` or `git diff --cached`
- Suggest the command: `git add <files> && git commit -m "<message>"`
- **This Skill must never execute `git commit` or `git push`**

finding_verdicts.reason: This is Markdown inline code describing a fixed git status command, not Ruby backtick execution. The command is read-only and has no user-controlled shell construction.
This is Markdown inline code for fixed git diff variants, not Ruby execution. The commands inspect repository diffs and do not include dynamic shell input.
The skill asks to suggest a command to the user, not execute it. The placeholder command requires user review and is bounded by notes saying execution is user's discretion.
This line prohibits running git commit or git push. The static match is only Markdown inline code around command names.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages from complex diffs can slow reviews. This skill inspects Git changes and drafts Conventional Commit messages with suggested file groups.
actual_capabilities: Checks changed files with git status.
Reads staged or unstaged diffs with git diff.
Creates English Conventional Commit headers and bullet summaries.
Suggests logical commit splits when changes span multiple concerns.
Provides git add and git commit command suggestions for user review.
limitations: It does not execute git commit or git push.
It depends on available Git diff context.
It cannot verify project-specific commit rules unless provided.
It may need user judgment when a diff contains unrelated changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Clean Commits
use_cases.description: Generate a clear message before committing staged changes.

use_cases.title: Split Mixed Changes
use_cases.description: Identify separate commit groups when one diff covers several concerns.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Context
use_cases.description: Turn file changes into concise commit summaries for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Basic Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Conventional Commit message for my current Git changes. Keep it in English and do not commit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Use Staged Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use before committing staged files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commit message with a short bullet summary.

prompt_templates.title: Check Commit Split
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use when changes may cover multiple topics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Git diff and tell me whether these changes should be split into multiple commits. Include target files and messages.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate commit suggestions that follow Conventional Commits and these project rules: [add rules]. Include rationale for any split.

output_examples.input: Staged changes update setup documentation and clarify install steps.
output_examples.output:
docs: update setup instructions

- Clarifies installation steps
- Adds setup notes for new contributors

output_examples.input: A diff adds a settings screen and refactors shared button styles.
output_examples.output:
Suggested split:

feat: add account settings screen

refactor: simplify shared button styles

output_examples.input: Changes fix a validation bug in the sign-in form.
output_examples.output:
fix: correct sign-in validation

- Handles empty email input
- Shows validation feedback before submit

best_practices: Stage related files before asking for a final message.
Share project commit conventions when they differ from Conventional Commits.
Review suggested file groups before copying any command.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to commit or push changes.
Do not combine unrelated features and refactors into one commit.
Do not accept a message without checking sensitive diff content.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly says commits and pushes must stay under user control.

faq.question: What commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It uses Conventional Commits with an English header and optional bullet summary.

faq.question: Can it work with staged changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect staged diffs when they are available.

faq.question: Can it split large changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend multiple focused commits when changes cover separate concerns.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Should I review the generated message?
faq.answer: Yes. Review the message and file grouping before using any suggested command.
